request: client contacts can be invited to an organization, raise and receive requests, and see nothing else
note: spec-slice --profile sharded produced 0 shards and left every id S-01..S-58 unassigned, so this pass answered all of them directly; the criteria map below is mine and no shard's. Currency (S-01..S-08) was judged against the state the spec was written on, run baseRef de9c5f916fa328734ed5f8f9c77023e8720e35e8, because this branch already carries an implementation of this very spec (771451a) and judging the spec's 'new' claims against code the spec itself produced would be circular. Where a claim is about code this spec did not write, the working tree and that baseline agree. scripts/spec-lint.mjs reports the bundle clean (41 requirements, 42 cases, 16 routes, 28 messages, 32 testids), so requirement-to-case joins, declared statuses and messages, decision-table domains and cited paths are settled mechanically and were not re-derived here.

findings.claim: the unconditional invariant that no account holds both principals has a live violator this bundle neither fixes, carves out nor scopes out: the shipping staff invitation gives a client contact a Membership without ever looking at ClientMembership

witness.detail: Invariant 1 (:357) is unconditional: 'An account never holds an active `Membership` and an active `ClientMembership` at once.' REQ-03-002's decision table (:88) rests on it — the (active, active) cell reads 'Unreachable — an accept that would write the second row is refused by REQ-03-014, and no other writer creates one.' There is another writer. `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/invitations` checks only memberships (invitations.service.ts:92-94: `include: { memberships: { where: { organizationId, status: 'active' } } }`), so a client contact's address can be invited as staff; `acceptExistingAccount` then writes `membership.create({ ... status: 'active' })` (invitations.service.ts:280-290, and again at :341 for the org-switch path) with no read of any client row. Sequence, entirely through routes this bundle leaves untouched: invite and accept a contact (REQ-03-012), then invite that same address as a `user` and accept — the account now holds an active `Membership` and an active `ClientMembership`, the cell the table calls unreachable, and REQ-03-002 has no answer for which principal signs in. REQ-03-014 (:158) guards only the client-invitation accept, which is the other direction.

findings.suggestedFix: state the staff side of the rule in this document: what `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/invitations` answers for an address holding an active `ClientMembership`, and what `POST /api/invitations/accept` answers when a staff invitation is accepted by an account that holds one — with the status and the named message for each — or name the staff invitation path out of scope and drop the word 'unconditional' from invariant 1 and the 'no other writer' clause from REQ-03-002's table.

findings.symbol: Roles & Permission Matrix row 2 / Routes / request-new-assignee-client
findings.claim: the matrix grants a `user` the right to raise a request to a client contact, and no route in the bundle lets a `user` — or anybody — read the contacts the picker must draw

witness.detail: The matrix (contracts:11) marks 'Raise a request, to a colleague or to a client contact' ✅ for `user`. The screens draw the contact picker for that same actor: `request-new-assignee-client` is 'present when the client addressee kind is chosen' (contracts:376) and the modal 'replaces the member picker with the contact picker' (contracts:449), the option carrying 'the client name under each option' (contracts, Screens). The only route in the bundle that returns contacts is `GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/clients/{clientId}/contacts`, guarded by `ViewClients` (contracts:34) — which a `user` does not hold: `ROLE_CAPABILITIES.user = ['CreateRequest', 'ViewOwnRequests']` (packages/validation/src/roles.ts:180) and `CAPABILITY_MATRIX.user['view-clients'] = false` (packages/validation/src/index.ts, user row). It is also keyed by `clientId`, which the requester cannot enumerate for the same reason, and the picker's set spans clients while the route's set is one client. TC-03-E2E-04 (cases:647) asserts that picker filling and the project control narrowing to 'projects of that contact's client that the requester is assigned to'; nothing in the bundle serves either list.

findings.suggestedFix: add the route the requester's picker reads — audience, request, response, statuses and messages — gated on a capability a `user` holds (the create-request right, not the client book), returning the contacts a requester may address with the client name on each; or change the matrix so only holders of `ViewClients` may address a client contact, and say in the screens that the picker is not drawn for anybody else.

findings.claim: two answers for one call: REQ-03-019 makes every organization route this spec does not grant a client principal answer 404, while REQ-03-027 and REQ-03-032 make two such routes answer 403

witness.detail: REQ-03-019 (:200-203): 'IF a client principal calls an organization route this spec does not grant them, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer `404`.' The matrix withholds both create and grant from a client contact (contracts:11 'Raise a request…' ❌; contracts:16 'Mark a request granted' ❌), so both are routes 'this spec does not grant them'. REQ-03-027 (:260-263) requires `403` with `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.clientCannotCreate` on the create route, and REQ-03-032 (:297-300) requires `403` with `REQUEST_MESSAGES.notYoursToGrant` on the grant route; the Routes table (contracts:36, :43) and edge cases 9 and 10 (contracts:517-518) repeat the 403s, and TC-03-INT-14 and TC-03-INT-22 assert them. No implementation answers both 404 and 403 for the same request, and the boundary of 'does not grant them' is nowhere drawn — the Security section (contracts:531-534) restates the 404 as covering 'every organization route this spec does not grant them', which is the same sentence.

findings.suggestedFix: bound REQ-03-019 by naming what it covers — every organization route outside the request routes named in this spec — and say in it that the create and grant routes answer 403 with the messages REQ-03-027 and REQ-03-032 give, so one rule states the whole answer for a client principal.

findings.claim: three shipping request routes can act on a request carrying this spec's new addressee kind, and the bundle gives none of them a rule, a Routes row or a line of scope

witness.detail: `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId}/reassign` (requests.controller.ts:167, `@RequireCapability('ViewAllRequests')`), `PATCH /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId}` (:75) and `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId}/cancel` (:151) all ship today and all write to a request row. None appears in the Routes table (contracts:29-47), and `grep -n reassign specs/requests/03-client-participants*.md` returns only REQ-03-035 (:316), Known Gaps (:381) and contracts edge case 5 (:509) — none of which says what the route does with a client-addressed request. Meanwhile REQ-03-035 (:316) requires a reassignment and a cancellation to write one outbox row per recipient, so both are live events of this feature, and the Data Model (contracts:248) requires `assigneeClientMembershipId` to be 'Required while `assigneeKind` is `client`, null otherwise' — an invariant a reassign that knows nothing of the column breaks by leaving it set. `PATCH` is the other half: if `projectId` or the addressee is editable after creation, REQ-03-021, REQ-03-022 and REQ-03-023 are gates a caller steps around one request later. Cancel is also the one request route with no row in the permission matrix, so what it answers a client principal is unstated as well.

findings.suggestedFix: give each of the three a Routes row and one rule: what reassign answers when the request it locks is addressed to a client (and what it writes to `assigneeClientMembershipId` and who it notifies), which fields PATCH may still change on a client-addressed request, and what cancel answers a client principal — or one line each placing them out of scope, which the reader can then rely on.

findings.claim: for an account holding a removed contact row, accepting an invitation to any other client requires a second ClientMembership that the table's own unique constraint forbids

witness.detail: contracts:224 declares `accountId` `String` `@unique` — 'One client contact per account'. REQ-03-012 (:148-151) says an accepted `client` invitation 'SHALL create an active `ClientMembership`', and the state table's `none | accept` row (contracts:205) says 'A valid token with no existing row writes an active `ClientMembership`'; the `removed | accept` row (contracts:211) restores an existing row, which is the same client's row. Reachable sequence with no rule against it: invite, accept and remove a contact of client X (REQ-03-006); invite the same address to client Y — REQ-03-013 (:153-156) refuses only an *active* row 'of the named client', so the invitation is written; the account accepts — REQ-03-014 (:158-162) refuses only an *active* `Membership` or `ClientMembership`, so the accept proceeds; the write then violates the uniqueness the Data Model declares. The Out of Scope bullet 'A contact belonging to more than one client' (:371) states an intention and refuses no write.

findings.suggestedFix: make REQ-03-013 and REQ-03-014 speak about a `ClientMembership` in any state rather than an active one — naming the status and message each answers when the row exists and is removed — or say in REQ-03-012 that an accept moves the account's existing row to the newly named client, and give the state table a row for it.

findings.claim: the recipient set of every notification turns on 'party to the request', which this bundle never defines and explicitly leaves in an earlier spec

witness.detail: REQ-03-036 (:322): 'THE SYSTEM SHALL make the recipients of an event every party to the request other than the principal who caused it.' REQ-03-028's Decided (:277-280) hands the definition away — 'the party test is already the whole of the read rule' — and the bundle nowhere says who the parties of a request are. Cover that sentence, as the reference test asks, and REQ-03-035's seven events (:316) have no determinable recipient list: for `reassigned`, whether the outgoing addressee is still a party decides whether the person losing the request is told; for `cancelled` and `granted` the same question decides whether anyone but the requester is written at all; and AC-9 ('one outbox row per recipient') and AC-10 cannot be checked against a set nobody has stated. TC-03-INT-24 and TC-03-INT-25 (cases:465, :479) exercise only a two-party request, so the cases do not settle it either.

findings.suggestedFix: enumerate the parties of a request in this document — the requester, the addressee of whichever kind, and whoever else — and say for a reassignment whether the outgoing addressee is a recipient of that event.

findings.claim: the case asserts a 409 for an address invited to a different client that no requirement produces, and the message it asserts says the opposite of the situation it is asserted in

witness.detail: REQ-03-013 (:153-156) fires only 'IF the invited address already holds an active `ClientMembership` of the named client'. TC-03-INT-07 (cases:241-244) then invites the same address 'to a **different** client of the same organization' and expects: 'The second also answers `409`, because the account already holds its one client membership.' No rule in the bundle says that. Under the spec's own rules the second invitation is written (REQ-03-013's condition is false, REQ-03-010 is about archival) and the refusal only arrives later, at accept, as `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.principalConflict` (REQ-03-014). The Error Messages row makes it worse: `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.alreadyLinked` is 'This person is already a contact of this client' (contracts:164), which is untrue of a person who is a contact of a different one — while the case reasons that the message is the same 'so neither answer says which client the person belongs to'.

findings.suggestedFix: widen REQ-03-013 to any active `ClientMembership` of the organization, whichever client it names, and reword the `alreadyLinked` text so it is true of both — or drop the second half of TC-03-INT-07 and let that invitation be refused at accept, as the rules currently say.

findings.claim: the request asks that client contacts raise requests; the bundle refuses it with a rule and puts it out of scope

witness.detail: The request this pass was given reads 'client contacts can be invited to an organization, raise and receive requests, and see nothing else'. Invited is delivered (REQ-03-008..REQ-03-015), receive is delivered (REQ-03-028..REQ-03-034), see nothing else is delivered (REQ-03-018, REQ-03-019). Raise is inverted: REQ-03-027 (:260-263) answers a client principal `403` with `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.clientCannotCreate`, Out of Scope opens with 'A client raising a request. REQ-03-027 refuses it; the thread carries anything urgent' (:368), the matrix marks it ❌ (contracts:11), the screens withhold `requests-new-btn` (contracts:387), and AC-14 makes the refusal an acceptance criterion. The decision may well be the right one, but it reverses an explicit clause of the request and only a person can settle that.
witness.source: specs/requests/03-client-participants.md:368 and :262 against the request line recorded in this verdict

findings.suggestedFix: either state the rule that lets a client contact raise a request — who they may address, which topics, which project, what the create route answers them — or record in the Summary that the request's 'raise' clause was declined and by whom, so the exclusion is a decision a reader meets rather than an omission.

findings.claim: the validation table answers a contact id from another organization with a 400 message; the case that covers the same rule expects 404

witness.detail: Validation rule 6 (contracts:346) makes the whole constraint 'An active contact of the caller's organization' answer `REQUEST_MESSAGES.assigneeInactive`, and REQ-03-020 (:207-210) states the constraint with no status at all. TC-03-INT-32 (cases:558-570) expects the cross-organization contact to answer '`404`, identical to an id that does not exist, so contact ids cannot be probed across organizations', while REQ-03-025 (:250-253) claims `assigneeInactive` for the removed case. An implementer who follows rule 6 answers 400 with a message for an id belonging to another organization, which both fails the case and tells the caller that the id exists — the leak the case exists to prevent. The member half of this route already splits the two answers (requests.service.ts:371-381: not found or another organization → 404; inactive → 400 `assigneeInactive`), so the split is a rule the spec has to state rather than one it can leave to rule 6's single row.

findings.suggestedFix: split rule 6 into the two answers REQ-03-020 needs — a contact of another organization or no row at all is 404, an inactive contact of the caller's organization is 400 `REQUEST_MESSAGES.assigneeInactive` — and say the 404 in REQ-03-020 itself.

findings.symbol: Required data-testid Attributes — 'Every other id in the table above is new'
findings.claim: an id the bundle declares new is drawn today

witness.detail: contracts:400-407 lists the ids that 'are drawn today' and then says 'Every other id in the table above is new.' `request-new-submit` is in the table (contracts:382) and is not in that list, so the bundle calls it new; it is rendered today at apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/NewRequestModal.tsx:285 (`data-testid="request-new-submit"`), which is also the control spec 02 already withholds when the staff catalogue is empty — the very behaviour contracts:382 says is being asserted per audience.

findings.suggestedFix: move `request-new-submit` into the sentence's list of ids that are drawn today.

findings.symbol: Routes — the contacts routes' capability refusal
findings.claim: the new contacts routes answer 403 where the shipping clients module collapses the same refusal to 404

witness.detail: contracts:34-36 gives the contacts routes `403` `CLIENT_MESSAGES.forbidden` and `403` `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.inviteForbidden` for a caller without the client capability, and TC-03-INT-12 asserts them. apps/api/src/clients/clients.service.ts:354-375 does the opposite for the same capability on the parent resource: 'A missing capability collapses to 404 rather than 403'. So a `user` asking about client X gets 404 from `/clients/{clientId}` and 403 from `/clients/{clientId}/contacts`, which tells them the client exists. The newest spec governs; this is recorded so the change is confirmed as meant.

findings.suggestedFix: if the 404 discipline was meant to hold here, say so in the Routes table and in REQ-03-008; if not, nothing needs to change.

findings.symbol: Verification Plan — Bringing it up, Rehearsal
findings.claim: the recorded commands pin the E2E ports

witness.detail: cases:14, :79 and :105 record `E2E_WEB_PORT=3100 E2E_API_PORT=4100`. The criterion's source (.claude/skills/spec/references/checklist.md:124) says the Verification Plan records 'never a port … The harness chooses those'. Judged clear rather than blocked because those are the ports CLAUDE.md itself tells an agent to run on and the suite steps them by 100 when they are busy, so nothing is sent at a server this repository does not publish — but the values buy the plan nothing and could go.

findings.suggestedFix: drop the two assignments from the recorded commands; the rest of the row still says what was walked.

findings.symbol: UI Description — contacts empty state, client requests empty state
findings.claim: two user-visible strings are described rather than given, so no case can assert either and the implementer invents the words

witness.detail: The UI table asks for '`client-contacts-empty-state` with a line saying what a contact is for' and, for a client principal with no requests, 'the requests empty state, with copy that does not mention scopes or filters they do not have'. Neither names an export, and the Error Messages table carries no row for either; `CLIENT_MESSAGES.emptyState` and `REQUEST_MESSAGES.emptyMine` are the precedents for both being exports. TC-03-E2E-05 asserts `client-contacts-empty-state` absent and nothing asserts its text.

findings.suggestedFix: give each string and the export that holds it.

findings.claim: three edge cases have no case and no line saying they have none

witness.detail: Edge case 4 (the client is archived while a contact is signed in — the contact keeps their session and their open requests), 6 (the requester is unassigned from the project after raising, and the request is unaffected) and 14 (a recipient's principal is removed before delivery, and the row is marked `skipped` with no address looked up) name behaviour no test case in cases.md asserts. Every other numbered row has one.

findings.suggestedFix: add a case for each, or one line per row saying it has none and why.

findings.claim: the lock is stated for a request's status write and for no other row two writers of this spec share

witness.detail: Invariant 4 (:361) states `FOR UPDATE` for every write of a request's status. Nothing is said about the row this spec adds: an accept (REQ-03-012) and a removal (REQ-03-006) both write the same `ClientMembership`, and an invite (REQ-03-011) and a second invite both write the same address's pending invitations. Either a line saying no lock is needed because the unique key and the transaction settle it, or the lock.

findings.symbol: Retry policy / GET requests — amended / ClientMembership.invitedByMembershipId
findings.claim: three small holes an implementer must fill by guessing

witness.detail: (a) The retry policy says a row 'is retried only from `failed` and only while `attempts` is below its bound' and never gives the bound — and nothing in the bundle ever fires a retry, since `deliver` is called once after the commit and no drain is specified. (b) The amended list response fixes `counts.waitingOnMe` for a client principal and says nothing about `counts.total`, which today's route also returns (requests.service.ts:255) and TC-03-INT-23 does not pin. (c) `ClientMembership.invitedByMembershipId` (contracts:229) is described as 'Audit' and no rule or case says who writes it or when.
witness.source: specs/requests/03-client-participants.contracts.md Retry policy, :229 and the amended list section

findings.suggestedFix: give the bound or say nothing retries in this spec; say what `counts.total` is for a client principal; name the write of `invitedByMembershipId`.

findings.claim: the matrix's last row grants every staff role a reach the product does not give them

witness.detail: 'Reach any organization screen other than requests' is ✅ for admin, manager, user and viewer. A `viewer` reaches neither Projects nor Clients nor Time Tracking today — Sidebar.tsx:59, :95, :103 gate all three on capabilities `CAPABILITY_MATRIX` denies a viewer, and the routes behind them refuse. The row's real subject is the client contact's ❌, which REQ-03-018 and REQ-03-019 already state.

findings.suggestedFix: narrow the row to what it is about — a client contact reaches no organization screen other than requests — or drop it.

findings.symbol: principal kind `member` vs the stored role value `member`
findings.claim: one word carries two vocabularies in the same bundle

witness.detail: `principal: "member"` (the amended `GET /api/me`), `assigneeKind` `member`, `authorKind` `member` and `recipientKind` `member` are principal kinds, while `member` is also a value `Membership.role` holds today (CLAUDE.md — Role values; normalizeRole maps it to `user`). Nothing in the bundle is wrong because of it, and a reader checking an authorization rule has to work out which vocabulary a `member` belongs to each time.

findings.suggestedFix: one line where the principal kinds are first enumerated, saying the kind `member` is not the stored role value `member`.

criteriaNotes.S-01: Every symbol named as existing exists: SessionGuard and OrgScopeGuard at the cited paths, MailService as an abstract class used as its own DI token (apps/api/src/mail/mail.service.ts:152), normalizeRole/hasCapability/ROLE_CAPABILITIES (roles.ts:38, :240, :116), can/CAPABILITY_MATRIX (index.ts:785, :642), the e2e helpers signupOrg, inviteAndAcceptViaApi, assignProjectMembersViaApi, latestInvitationToken and createBareAccount, and apps/api/test/{clients,requests,session-revocation}.spec.ts with overrideProvider(MailService) at clients.spec.ts:136.
criteriaNotes.S-02: Every quoted message matches its export character for character: AUTH_MESSAGES.deactivated and invalidCredentials, INVITE_MESSAGES.tokenInvalid, CLIENT_MESSAGES.clientArchived and forbidden, REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.pickerEmpty and the fourteen REQUEST_MESSAGES rows. The CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES rows are declared new and are judged against the baseline; the export exists in the working tree only because this branch carries this spec's own implementation, whose alreadyLinked wording differs — that difference is reported as R7 on its own merits, not as a currency claim.
criteriaNotes.S-03: Statuses attributed to shipping routes hold at the baseline: create 201, messages 201, answer/grant/decline 200, login 400 with the deactivated message, accept 200, GET /api/me 200 with a null body for an account holding no membership (me.controller.ts:27).
criteriaNotes.S-04: Schema facts hold: Invitation.role is a free-form String with no clientId column, Request.assigneeKind exists with a nullable assigneeMembershipId, RequestMessage.authorKind, RequestEvent.actorKind and its label snapshots, Account.securityStamp, ProjectMember and Project.clientId.
criteriaNotes.S-05: Blocked by R10 only. Every other 'today' claim verified: /api/me answers null for an account with no membership; the create route's capability check is its first statement (requests.service.ts:324) and its 400s are decided body, topic, audience, addressee, project in that order; nav-members is drawn unconditionally while every other row asks a capability a null role is refused (Sidebar.tsx:72-105, viewer holding only ViewOwnRequests); the modal reads audience=staff today (NewRequestModal.tsx:165) and fills its addressee picker from /members (:145); the two seeded client topics are Access (access, 10) and Other (question, 20) (request-topics.seed.ts:37-38); the mail sink names the type 'invitation' (mail.service.ts:129).
criteriaNotes.S-06: Select, Toggle and Input are exported by apps/web/src/ds.ts; SelectOption.label is React.ReactNode (1_DS for dev/components/forms/Select.d.ts:3), so the DS gaps table's 'None' holds for both controls this spec adds.
criteriaNotes.S-08: scripts/spec-lint.mjs reports clean: 41 requirements, 42 cases, 16 routes, 28 messages, 32 testids, matching the bundle's own counts.
criteriaNotes.S-15: Every rule has its column. The one column written by no stated rule is ClientMembership.invitedByMembershipId, which is note-level and is reported in N6.
criteriaNotes.S-26: The authorization rules this spec adds do not key on a role: the client principal holds none (REQ-03-016, REQ-03-017), and the manage-clients gate resolves through helpers whose answer for the stored value `member` is already fixed in code — CAPABILITY_MATRIX has no `member` row so can() answers false, and normalizeRole maps `member` to `user`, whose set holds neither ViewClients nor ManageClients. Both readings refuse, so nothing turns on the omission; the vocabulary collision it creates is reported as N8.
criteriaNotes.S-28: Each E2E case reaches something an API test cannot: the mail-to-session journey, navigation rows that must not be drawn, the shell's redirect after a revoked session, the modal's per-audience re-read and focus, and the client's action controls. No existing e2e covers revocation on removal (grep over e2e/tests). Every server rule they touch also has an integration case.
criteriaNotes.S-31: Each route names its audience, statuses and messages. The DELETE contacts route gives no response body, which TC-03-INT-10 does not need; judged clear rather than blocked because the removal's observable effects are stated in REQ-03-006 and the case.
criteriaNotes.S-34: No TBD and no requirement without behaviour. The retry policy's unstated bound is reported as N6: no path in this spec ever retries, so nothing an implementer must build turns on it.
criteriaNotes.S-35: n/a — the Access table records that the shipped notifier makes no outbound call, so there is no external system and no credential.
criteriaNotes.S-40: Judged clear; the pinned ports are reported as N2.
criteriaNotes.S-42: The additions beyond the request — the notification port, its outbox table and the four new columns — are named in the Summary as additions.
criteriaNotes.S-53: Migrations are declared additive with no new NOT NULL, but deploy-order independence — the previous image still serving against the new schema — is nowhere stated in words.
criteriaNotes.S-54: n/a — no boundary value is shared with an external system.
